description.value: The study compared chronic prescription opioid users with chronic pain with healthy controls using resting-state functional connectivity and voxel-based morphometry to examine frontostriatal abnormalities and their relationships with affect and opioid misuse.

spans.text: The current study utilized functional and structural imaging techniques to compare a group of prescription opioid users with chronic pain (OUG) ( N =31) to drug-free healthy controls ( N =30).

value: We hypothesized that prescription opioid users with chronic pain, as compared to healthy control subjects, would evidence weaker frontostriatal rsFC coupled with less frontostriatal gray matter volume (GMV).
Further, that those opioid use-related deficits in frontostriatal circuitry would be associated with the negative affect and drug misuse.

spans.text: We hypothesized that the OUG, as compared to healthy control subjects, would evidence weaker frontostriatal rsFC and less frontostriatal GMV that would in turn be significantly associated with the magnitude of affective disturbances and opioid misuse.

spans.text: All functional and structural images were preprocessed using the computational anatomy 12 (CAT12 - www.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat ) and statistical parametric mapping 12 (SPM12 - http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/software/spm12/ ) MATLAB 2018a toolboxes according to a standard pipeline employing default settings

Pre-processing of resting-state fMRI images included: slice-time correction (for non-multiband data) and realignment; motion outlier detection (framewise displacement > 1mm) www.nitrc.org/projects/artifact_detect ) and correction (via nearest-neighbor interpolation); coregistration of functional images to structural image; warping to MNI space using forward deformations and resampling to (1.5mm) 3 voxel size (i.e., 3.375µL).
All preprocessed fMRI images and segmented tissue maps were smoothed with a (10mm) 3 FWHM Gaussian filter prior to modeling
